summary_for_children: Al-Mulk means The Dominion. It invites us to look at the sky again and again and find no flaw, to see the birds held up by Allah, and to walk the earth He made easy for us.
world_title: Seven Skies and the Outspread Wings
environment_concept: A sky without flaw to look at again and again (67:3-4), slopes to walk (67:15) and birds with outspread wings (67:19).
architecture_and_scenery: Seven layered skies, wide slopes, flocks of birds.

palette.lighting: Clear sky with stars at dusk

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Kingdom of the Skies
story_library.children_narration: Look up at the night sky. Can you count all the stars? Surah Al-Mulk invites us to look again and again at creation and reflect on its order. It also reminds us how important water is to life.

world_idea.title: The Celestial Observatory
world_idea.description: Explore a planetarium-style environment, examine stars and clouds, and learn about water through interactive scientific exhibits connected to the surah.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
